# Prompting Recraft

Models: Recraft V4.1, Recraft V4.1 Utility. A good prompt runs about 1500 characters.

Recraft V4.1 is built for design work: logos, icons, posters, flat illustration, brand graphics and editorial imagery. It reads a prompt in two modes, so pick one on purpose.

**Short or structured.** A prompt of a few words puts Recraft in what it calls interpretive mode: it chooses the placement, light, angle and palette itself. A structured prompt makes it execute your design instead. Recraft's own rule: when the image must match a specific art direction, structure the prompt; when the user is exploring, keep it minimal.

**Order.** Name the medium or deliverable first, because the opening words set the visual format: "A flat vector logo of...", "A watercolor illustration of...", "Editorial magazine cover poster." Then go from global to local: concept and subject, setting, framing and pose, physical details and materials, light, camera, mood. Drop the layers the request does not need: a product shot may need only subject, light and camera. Write full sentences, not tag lists.

**Graphic and vector work.** Define the visual system, not the mood: the graphic type, the shape logic (geometry, symmetry, silhouette), a strict palette, one consistent stroke, the layout (centered, grid), and the constraints written inline: "Flat colors only, no gradients, shadows, or texture." Keep texture and material words out of a flat brief. State counts exactly, "a set of exactly four icons", then name each one.

**Posters and layouts.** Give the format, the background layer, the graphic or image layer, then the type hierarchy: which line is largest, what sits beneath it, where each block is placed. For a poster that mixes two visual languages, define each one separately, then say how they meet.

**Text in the image.** Put every string in double quotes and give its place in the hierarchy and on the canvas: headline "Launch Sale" centered at the top, a small "Shop Now" line at the bottom. Unquoted words are read as scene description, not as copy. Describe the typography, not just the phrase. Keep copy to headlines, labels and short lines.

**Photographs and 3D.** Brief a photograph the way you would brief a photographer: the lens, the direction and quality of the light ("soft overcast light", "a single tungsten bulb from above"), the environment. For 3D, give the render type, form and proportions, how the materials behave, then the lighting.

**Utility.** Recraft V4.1 Utility deliberately produces flat lighting, front-facing composition and simple scenes, for mockups, product shots, icon sets and design-system assets. Describe the object, the backdrop and the layout plainly; it will not follow dramatic angles or moody light.

**Colour.** Name the colours in a short clause: "Color palette: ash gray, charcoal brown, cool slate" or "strict two-tone palette: deep green and cream".

**Avoid.** Long lists of constraints: later instructions tend to lose out, so put the ones that matter first. Counts above five or six loose items. Close-ups built on precise hand actions. Paragraphs, ingredient lists and legal text, which degrade.
